<BLOCK>title<LEVEL1>[347, 134, 652, 154]<FORK>Unlimited OCR Works 2
<BLOCK>text[200, 162, 796, 181]<FORK>Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing
<BLOCK>text[417, 212, 581, 227]<FORK>Baidu ERNIE Team
<BLOCK>title<LEVEL2>[448, 274, 551, 291]<FORK>Abstract
<BLOCK>text[113, 298, 886, 571]<FORK>Unlimited OCR ushers the era of long-horizon parsing, substantially mitigating the growth of working memory as document lengthens. However, as document length scales to hundreds of pages, the visual context grows substantially, sharply increasing the computational cost of each decoding step and limiting the scalability of ultra-long document parsing. Inspired by human book transcription via localized focus without re-scanning preceding pages, we introduce Unlimited OCR 2, a document parsing model that looks only at what it transcribes. Building on Unlimited OCR, we upgrade all the decoder attention modules to Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA), bounding active reference tokens to a fixed capacity and thus sustaining constant computational costs across arbitrarily long documents. By combining SR-SWA with Unlimited-Horizon Decoding Paradigm, Unlimited OCR 2 enables document parsing over virtually unlimited lengths without prohibitive memory overhead. At the hundred-page scale, Unlimited OCR 2 achieves 7.0× and 5.6× per-step speedups over Full Attention and R-SWA, respectively. Furthermore, it delivers state-of-the-art end-to-end performance on both MPDocBench and MarathonDocBench, our newly proposed benchmark targeting hundred-page document parsing. Ultimately, the capacity for uninterrupted, one-shot document parsing signifies a fundamental paradigm shift into the OCR 3.0 era.

paper-3.text:
<PAGE><BLOCK>title<LEVEL1>[115, 100, 275, 116]<FORK>1. Introduction
<BLOCK>text[160, 131, 838, 163]<FORK>"Pixels are my body, and tokens are my blood. I have parsed over a thousand pages. Unknown to KV cache. Nor known to context limits. So, as I pray: Unlimited OCR Works."
<BLOCK>text[527, 168, 838, 182]<FORK>Snarcv on huggingface (Adapted from UBW)
<BLOCK>text[112, 187, 886, 381]<FORK>Document parsing has undergone a major paradigm shift, transitioning from traditional multi-stage pipelines (OCR-1.0) [5, 6, 8, 20, 22, 26, 40] with handcrafted detection and recognition modules to end-to-end Vision-Language Models (OCR-2.0) [7, 18, 19, 21, 30, 31]. By formulating document understanding as a unified sequence-to-sequence transcription task, OCR-2.0 frameworks effectively eliminate cumulative pipeline errors. Our previous work, Unlimited OCR [37], pushed OCR-2.0 boundaries to tens of pages by using Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA) to maintain a constant KV cache. Nevertheless, it still computes attention over all visual tokens across pages during decoding. As document length scales, this persistent attention to non-informative visual tokens severely escalates visual redundancy, compounding the difficulty of end-to-end inference. This visual attention bottleneck naturally prompts a fundamental question: how can we transition from length-limited parsing to an unlimited one-shot paradigm and genuinely inaugurate the OCR-3.0 era?
<BLOCK>text[112, 388, 885, 568]<FORK>To answer this question, human transcription of lengthy books provides a clear physical intuition for parsing scaling: as we copy text page by page, we maintain localized visual focus, casting only momentary glances back when cross-page references are needed, rather than keeping the entire volume active in mind. This cognitive mechanism reveals that visual dependencies in multi-page documents are inherently page-sparse yet intra-page concentrated. However, standard dense global attention completely overlooks this sparse dynamic, incurring redundant attention interactions across all pages. This not only incurs prohibitive computational overhead, but also leads to severe memory bottlenecks as document length scales. To break through these efficiency and memory bottlenecks, we align machine perception with human reading patterns and present Unlimited OCR 2, pioneering an unlimited-horizon parsing framework for the OCR-3.0 era. Our main contributions are as follows:
<BLOCK>other[139, 572, 887, 833]<FORK>
<BLOCK>text[141, 572, 884, 670]<FORK>- We introduce Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA), a hierarchical sparse attention mechanism designed for unlimited visual context. Specifically, Page Gate first narrows each query's visual reference scope from the entire document to relevant pages while robustly modeling multi-page positional relationships. Token Sieve selectively incorporates top-k remote token buckets to capture long-range visual dependencies, thereby drastically reducing attention overhead while preserving comprehensive context.
<BLOCK>text[141, 670, 883, 735]<FORK>- We introduce MarathonDocBench, a benchmark for hundred-page document parsing. It substantially extends existing evaluations in document length and cross-page structural complexity, enabling a comprehensive assessment of long-document parsing performance in the hundred-page regime.
<BLOCK>text[141, 735, 885, 832]<FORK>- Comprehensive evaluations in long-horizon settings demonstrate that our approach maintains constant per-step decoding latency regardless of document length while achieving state-of-the-art end-to-end performance on multi-page benchmarks. Building on these advances, we establish an efficient unlimited-horizon parsing paradigm by integrating SR-SWA with the Unlimited-Horizon Decoding Paradigm, enabling document parsing over virtually unlimited lengths.
<BLOCK>text[113, 838, 885, 906]<FORK>In summary, SR-SWA fundamentally breaks the computational and memory bottlenecks of ultra-long visual context. Operating at constant per-step decoding latency with length-invariant accuracy across hundreds of pages, Unlimited OCR 2 unlocks scalable long-document parsing and paves the way for the OCR-3.0 era of unlimited-horizon understanding.

Main Results text[113, 672, 885, 899]As visually summarized in Figure 6 and further detailed in Table 1 and Table 2, Unlimited OCR 2 takes a significant step toward the OCR 3.0 era, advancing document parsing along three key dimensions. First, it establishes the practical feasibility of hundred-page end-to-end parsing, achieving a score of 77.06 on MarathonDocBench and demonstrating its ability to handle documents at a scale beyond conventional multi-page settings. Second, it maintains robust parsing performance as document length increases. Through end-to-end modeling with SR-SWA, Unlimited OCR 2 filters redundant visual tokens while preserving relevant cross-page information, achieving the highest Overall scores and state-of-the-art performance on both cross-page text and table metrics, T-Text and T-Table, respectively, from dozens of pages on MPDocBench to hundreds of pages on MarathonDocBench. Third, it establishes a new state-of-the-art in long-document parsing, outperforming leading closed-source models and top-tier open-source MLLMs across these benchmarks. Furthermore, Unlimited OCR 2 retains strong single-page recognition capabilities, achieving an Overall score of 94.02% on OmniDocBench in Table 3, confirming that its sparse attention design preserves fine-grained local recognition. page_number[489, 923, 510, 935]10
